changelog.en:
# Changelog

## 1.0.0 - 2026-10-30

- First stable version: the plugin is no longer marked as beta (`stage: stable`).
- The bench pictures (`preview.yaml`) name the cover file for `/local/cover.jpg`; `store.png` shows the layout of
  0.14.3.

## 0.14.3 - 2026-10-30

- The tempo line stands under the album, no longer above it.
- The small volume display sits at the right end of the line over the progress bar, beside the time, no longer at
  the title's right; the title gets the whole width.
- The small volume display and the time are one font size larger.

## 0.14.2 - 2026-10-30

- Builds on Tessera 0.4.91 and later (plugin API 0.24), which took away the key and value form of `tessera::action`:
  the volume, the seek and the mute send their fields as a JSON object, a number and a true or false. The manifest names
  plugin API 0.12, which brought those fields.
- Setup in the README has a fourth step: the screen must be allowed to perform Home Assistant actions, or the
  buttons do nothing.

## 0.14.1 - 2026-10-28

- The pause display now covers the whole tile, also the ends of the progress bar in the corners.
- The pause sign is drawn larger: two thirds of the tile's height instead of the size of an icon.

## 0.14.0 - 2026-10-19

- The buttons show Tessera's icons (previous, play, pause, next, quieter, louder, speaker) instead of signs such as
  "<<" and "||".
- The speaker of the volume display shows volume-high, or volume-off while muted. The icons for a low and a medium
  volume are not in Tessera's set, so below 67 % the speaker showed nothing.
- A title, an artist or an album that is too wide now ends in dots instead of running as a marquee, as every label of
  the screen. The tile no longer keeps the screen drawing while it is on the glass.
- The tempo line ("138 BPM") comes from the translations.
- The tile keeps its texts in the memory beside the chip (PSRAM) where the board has it, not inside the chip.
- The README says which board SCMT was tried on.

## 0.13.0 - 2026-10-18

- New option "Colour of the bars" for the progress bar and the volume bar: the screen's accent (default, as before),
  green, amber, red, blue, purple, or like the text. These are the core's colours, readable in light and dark; Tessera
  allows no colour of your own.
- "Album name" and "Tempo" are now one option, "Extra lines" (none, album, tempo, or both), to make room for the colour
  (a tile has at most 12 options). Tiles that had the two switches keep what they showed.

## 0.12.1 - 2026-10-18

- The progress bar and the time no longer jump back and forth when a player reports a position a few seconds old as if
  it were new (HASS.Agent with Spotify). While the same track plays on, the tile keeps its own clock and follows a
  report only when it differs by more than 3 seconds (a seek); a new track, a pause or a start sets the clock anew.

## 0.12.0 - 2026-10-17

- New option "Tempo": the tempo of the music (for example "138 BPM") as a line under the artist. It comes from a sensor
  chosen per screen in Tessera (new input "Tempo sensor"), for example the one HASS.Agent makes from BPM2SCMT. After a
  new track the line waits until the sensor has the new tempo.
- The plugin now reads that one entity itself (permission `read_entities`); Tessera asks for it on the update.
- The README describes a new way to the cover for players whose own cover is refused: a template image in Home
  Assistant, shown with the "Cover address" `/api/image_proxy/image.scmt_cover?v={v}`. It replaces the cover
  automation with a file under `/local/`, which does not work with Tessera 0.4.88 (403). The plugin is unchanged there.

## 0.11.0 - 2026-10-17

- New option "Text size": small (as before 0.10.3), medium (default, as now) or large (artist and album one step
  larger, a long title runs in the large font).
- A tap on the progress bar always seeks; the option "Seek by tapping the bar" is gone.
- Mute comes with the volume buttons, between quieter and louder; the option "Mute" is gone. With the volume buttons,
  a tap on a volume display mutes too.

## 0.10.3 - 2026-10-17

- Larger text: the title in the large font of a card's value, artist and album in the font of a key's words. A long
  title gets smaller only down to the former size and then runs as a marquee; on a low tile everything steps down as
  before.
- Fix: text that runs as a marquee no longer runs over the cover or the card's edge.

## 0.10.2 - 2026-10-17

- The volume bar always stands at the right edge, also when the cover is at the right, and is a third narrower.
- Even spacing: the cover, the text, the progress bar and the buttons now stand as far apart as from the card's edge.

## 0.10.1 - 2026-10-17

- Fix: on a low tile (the small 2.8-inch screen) the artist no longer lies over the time. The title takes a smaller font
  when it is too high as well, and stands alone when there is no room for the artist.
- The README now says that the option "Cover address" and the cover automation do not work with the current Tessera
  app (0.4.88): it fetches `/local/` through the Supervisor, which refuses it (403), so the tile shows a grey block.
- The picture for the plugin store shows the new look.

## 0.10.0 - 2026-10-16

- A title, artist or album too wide for the tile runs as a marquee instead of being cut with dots.
- The volume bar stands upright along the edge of the tile, opposite the cover (at the right, or at the left when the
  cover is at the right). It now needs two columns instead of two rows.
- "Seek by tapping the bar" is on by default.
- Even spacing: the same gap between the cover, the text, the progress bar and the buttons, and the outer buttons line
  up with the edges.
- With the text at the top or the bottom, it lines up with the cover's upper or lower edge.

## 0.9.1 - 2026-10-16

- Fix: the manifest was refused ("tiles[0].options: at most 12 entries"), because the tile "SCMT" had 15 options.
  Three pairs are now one choice each, and nothing is lost:
  - "Album cover": left, right or off (was "Album cover" and "Cover position").
  - "Buttons": none, playback, volume, or both (was "Playback buttons" and "Volume buttons").
  - "Big display": none, volume, pause, or both (was "Big volume display" and "Pause display").
- Tiles placed with an older version keep their settings; the tile still reads the former options.

## 0.9.0 - 2026-10-16

- New option "Pause display": while the player is paused, a half see-through display with the pause sign lies over the
  whole tile.
- New option "Cover position": the album cover at the left or at the right of the text.
- New option "Position of the text": title, artist and album at the top, in the middle or at the bottom of the space
  beside the cover.
- More languages: French, Spanish, Italian and Dutch, beside English and German. The README and this changelog come in
  these languages too (`README.de.md`, `CHANGELOG.de.md`, and so on).
- The README describes the automation that brings an album cover to the display (experimental), with an example in
  `examples/cover_automation.yaml`.
- The tile reserves a little more memory for the new display.

## 0.8.1 - 2026-10-16

- The "Cover address" is now used exactly as typed. A `{v}` in it is replaced by a number that changes with every track
  (for example `/local/cover.jpg?v={v}`); before, that number was always added behind the address as `?v=`.
- The store picture `store.png` for the plugin store was added.

## 0.8.0 - 2026-10-15

- New option "Cover address": a fixed address of a cover file in Home Assistant (for example `/local/cover.jpg`), shown
  instead of the player's own picture. For players whose cover the tile may not fetch.

## 0.7.1 - 2026-10-15

- Fix: the build failed with "Component not found: now_playing", because `plugin.yaml` still named the old component. It
  now says `scmt`, the same as the manifest and the folder.

## 0.7.0 - 2026-10-15

- The plugin's id is now `scmt` (it was `now_playing`), the same as its folder and its component. The app sees a new
  plugin: remove the old one from the screen, add this one, and place its tiles again.

## 0.6.0 - 2026-10-15

- The plugin is called SCMT (Simple Customizable Media Tile). Its id, `now_playing`, stays, so tiles already on a screen
  keep working.
- New option "Height of the progress bar" (2 to 16 pixels, 4 by default).

## 0.5.0 - 2026-10-15

- New options: "Seek by tapping the bar", "Mute", "Volume bar" (a tap sets the volume), "Album name" (a third line).
- New option "Big volume display": a half see-through display over the whole tile for three seconds after a change, with
  the number in large digits and a speaker after it. The small volume display has a speaker too.
- The tile can be up to 4x4 cells (the editor offers what fits the screen's grid).
- Needs three more actions: `media_seek`, `volume_mute`, `volume_set`.

## 0.4.1 - 2026-10-14

- Fix: the manifest was refused because the choice value `off` was read as a truth value; every choice value is now
  written as text.

## 0.4.0 - 2026-10-14

- New: the option "Progress" now chooses a bar, the time (1:36 / 7:36), both, or nothing.
- New: the option "Volume display" shows the volume at the title's right: when it changes (three seconds), always, or
  never. A muted player shows "Muted".

## 0.3.2 - 2026-10-14

- The buttons in the tile have a light frame.

## 0.3.1 - 2026-10-14

- The cover place is shown only when the player has a picture the screen may fetch; otherwise the text takes the whole
  width, and no empty grey square stays.

## 0.3.0 - 2026-10-14

- New: the album cover beside the title (option "Album cover"), from two cells wide, on screens that show pictures.
- New: playback buttons (previous, play/pause, next) and volume buttons (quieter, louder) inside the tile, as options.
  They need a tile of two rows or more.
- Needs plugin API 0.10.

## 0.2.0 - 2026-10-14

- New: a progress bar on the tile (option "Progress bar", on by default), if the player reports duration and position.
- New: a tap on the tile plays or pauses.
- New: the tile "Media button" (previous, play/pause, next, louder, quieter), one tile per button.
- The tile can now be 1x1; it was 2x1 at least.

## 0.1.1 - 2026-10-14

- Fix: the build failed because the colours were written as `tessera::theme::`; they are `theme::`.

## 0.1.0 - 2026-10-14

- First version: shows the title and artist of a media player.

# Wijzigingenlogboek

## 1.0.0 - 2026-10-30

- Eerste stabiele versie: de plugin is niet langer als bèta gemarkeerd (`stage: stable`).
- De afbeeldingen van de testbank (`preview.yaml`) noemen het hoesbestand voor `/local/cover.jpg`; `store.png`
  toont de indeling van 0.14.3.

## 0.14.3 - 2026-10-30

- De tempo-regel staat onder het album, niet meer erboven.
- De kleine volumeweergave staat rechts op de regel boven de voortgangsbalk, naast de tijd, niet meer rechts van
  de titel; de titel krijgt de hele breedte.
- De kleine volumeweergave en de tijd zijn één lettergrootte groter.

## 0.14.2 - 2026-10-30

- Bouwt op Tessera 0.4.91 en nieuwer (plugin-API 0.24), waarin de vorm van `tessera::action` met sleutel en waarde
  is weggevallen: volume, spoelen en dempen sturen hun velden als JSON-object, als getal en als true of false. Het
  manifest noemt plugin-API 0.12, die deze velden bracht.
- Instellen in de README heeft een vierde stap: het scherm moet Home Assistant-acties mogen uitvoeren, anders doen
  de knoppen niets.

## 0.14.1 - 2026-10-28

- De pauzeweergave bedekt nu de hele tegel, ook de uiteinden van de voortgangsbalk in de hoeken.
- Het pauzeteken is groter: twee derde van de tegelhoogte in plaats van de grootte van een icoon.

## 0.14.0 - 2026-10-19

- De knoppen tonen de iconen van Tessera (vorige, afspelen, pauze, volgende, zachter, harder, luidspreker) in plaats van
  tekens als „<<” en „||”.
- De luidspreker van de volumeweergave toont volume-high, of volume-off als het gedempt is. De iconen voor een laag en
  een middelmatig volume zitten niet in de set van Tessera, dus onder 67 % toonde de luidspreker niets.
- Een te brede titel, artiest of album eindigt nu op puntjes in plaats van als lichtkrant te lopen, zoals elke tekst
  van het scherm. De tegel laat het scherm niet meer steeds tekenen zolang hij te zien is.
- De temporegel („138 BPM”) komt uit de vertalingen.
- De tegel bewaart zijn teksten in het geheugen naast de chip (PSRAM) als het bord dat heeft, niet in de chip.
- De README zegt op welk bord SCMT is geprobeerd.

## 0.13.0 - 2026-10-18

- Nieuwe optie „Kleur van de balken” voor de voortgangsbalk en de volumebalk: de accentkleur van het scherm
  (standaard, zoals eerder), groen, amber, rood, blauw, paars of zoals de tekst. Het zijn de kleuren van de kern,
  leesbaar in licht en donker; eigen kleuren staat Tessera niet toe.
- „Albumnaam” en „Tempo” zijn nu één optie, „Extra regels” (geen, album, tempo of beide), zodat de kleur erbij past
  (een tegel heeft hooguit 12 opties). Tegels met de twee schakelaars tonen hetzelfde als voorheen.

## 0.12.1 - 2026-10-18

- De voortgangsbalk en de tijd springen niet meer heen en weer wanneer een speler een positie van enkele seconden oud
  als nieuw meldt (HASS.Agent met Spotify). Zolang hetzelfde nummer doorspeelt, houdt de tegel een eigen klok bij en
  volgt een melding alleen als die meer dan 3 seconden afwijkt (spoelen); een nieuw nummer, een pauze of een start zet
  de klok opnieuw.

## 0.12.0 - 2026-10-17

- Nieuwe optie „Tempo”: het tempo van de muziek (bijvoorbeeld „138 BPM”) als regel onder de artiest. Het komt van een
  sensor die per scherm in Tessera wordt gekozen (nieuwe invoer „Temposensor”), bijvoorbeeld die welke HASS.Agent maakt
  van BPM2SCMT. Na een nieuw nummer wacht de regel tot de sensor het nieuwe tempo heeft.
- De plug-in leest die ene entiteit nu zelf (recht `read_entities`); Tessera vraagt erom bij de update.
- De README beschrijft een nieuwe weg naar de hoes voor spelers waarvan de eigen hoes wordt geweigerd: een
  sjabloonafbeelding in Home Assistant, getoond met het „Adres van de hoes” `/api/image_proxy/image.scmt_cover?v={v}`.
  Die vervangt de hoesautomatisering met een bestand onder `/local/`, dat niet werkt met Tessera 0.4.88 (403). De
  plug-in verandert daarvoor niet.

## 0.11.0 - 2026-10-17

- Nieuwe optie „Tekstgrootte”: klein (zoals vóór 0.10.3), middel (standaard, zoals nu) of groot (artiest en album een
  stap groter, een lange titel loopt in het grote lettertype).
- Een tik op de voortgangsbalk spoelt altijd; de optie „Spoelen door op de balk te tikken” vervalt.
- Dempen hoort bij de volumeknoppen, tussen zachter en harder; de optie „Dempen” vervalt. Met de volumeknoppen dempt
  ook een tik op een volumeweergave.

## 0.10.3 - 2026-10-17

- Grotere tekst: de titel in het grote lettertype van de waarde van een kaart, artiest en album in het lettertype van de
  woorden op een knop. Een lange titel wordt alleen tot de vroegere grootte kleiner en loopt daarna als lichtkrant; op
  een lage tegel wordt alles kleiner zoals voorheen.
- Reparatie: lichtkranttekst loopt niet meer over de hoes of de rand van de kaart.

## 0.10.2 - 2026-10-17

- De volumebalk staat altijd aan de rechterrand, ook als de hoes rechts staat, en is een derde smaller.
- Gelijke afstanden: hoes, tekst, voortgangsbalk en knoppen staan nu even ver van elkaar als van de rand van de kaart.

## 0.10.1 - 2026-10-17

- Reparatie: op een lage tegel (het kleine 2,8-inch-scherm) ligt de artiest niet meer over de tijd. De titel krijgt ook
  een kleiner lettertype als hij te hoog is, en staat alleen als er geen plaats is voor de artiest.
- De README zegt nu dat de optie „Adres van de hoes” en de hoesautomatisering niet werken met de huidige Tessera-app
  (0.4.88): die haalt `/local/` op via de Supervisor, en die weigert het (403), dus de tegel toont een grijs blok.
- De afbeelding voor de pluginwinkel toont het nieuwe uiterlijk.

## 0.10.0 - 2026-10-16

- Een titel, artiest of album die te breed is voor de tegel loopt als lichtkrant door in plaats van met puntjes te
  worden afgekapt.
- De volumebalk staat rechtop langs de rand van de tegel, tegenover de hoes (rechts, of links als de hoes rechts staat).
  Hij vraagt nu twee kolommen in plaats van twee rijen.
- „Spoelen door op de balk te tikken” staat standaard aan.
- Gelijke afstanden: dezelfde ruimte tussen hoes, tekst, voortgangsbalk en knoppen, en de buitenste knoppen sluiten
  gelijk met de randen.
- Staat de tekst boven of onderaan, dan sluit hij gelijk met de boven- of onderrand van de hoes.

## 0.9.1 - 2026-10-16

- Reparatie: het manifest werd geweigerd („tiles[0].options: at most 12 entries”), omdat de tegel „SCMT” 15 opties had.
  Drie paren zijn nu elk één keuze, zonder dat er iets verloren gaat:
  - „Albumhoes”: links, rechts of uit (was „Albumhoes” en „Positie van de hoes”).
  - „Knoppen”: geen, afspelen, volume of allebei (was „Afspeelknoppen” en „Volumeknoppen”).
  - „Grote weergave”: geen, volume, pauze of allebei (was „Grote volumeweergave” en „Pauzeweergave”).
- Tegels die met een oudere versie zijn geplaatst, houden hun instellingen; de tegel leest de vroegere opties nog steeds.

## 0.9.0 - 2026-10-16

- Nieuwe optie „Pauzeweergave”: zolang de speler gepauzeerd is, ligt een half doorzichtige weergave met het pauzeteken
  over de hele tegel.
- Nieuwe optie „Positie van de hoes”: de albumhoes links of rechts van de tekst.
- Nieuwe optie „Positie van de tekst”: titel, artiest en album boven, in het midden of onderaan de ruimte naast de hoes.
- Meer talen: Frans, Spaans, Italiaans en Nederlands, naast Engels en Duits. Ook de README en dit logboek bestaan in
  deze talen (`README.de.md`, `CHANGELOG.de.md`, enzovoort).
- De README beschrijft de automatisering die een albumhoes naar het scherm brengt (experimenteel), met een voorbeeld in
  `examples/cover_automation.yaml`.
- De tegel reserveert iets meer geheugen voor de nieuwe weergave.

## 0.8.1 - 2026-10-16

- Het „Adres van de hoes” wordt nu precies zo gebruikt als het is ingevoerd. Een `{v}` erin wordt vervangen door een
  getal dat bij elk nummer verandert (bijvoorbeeld `/local/cover.jpg?v={v}`); eerder werd dat getal altijd als `?v=`
  achter het adres gezet.
- De winkelafbeelding `store.png` voor de pluginwinkel is toegevoegd.

## 0.8.0 - 2026-10-15

- Nieuwe optie „Adres van de hoes”: een vast adres van een hoesbestand in Home Assistant (bijvoorbeeld
  `/local/cover.jpg`), getoond in plaats van de eigen afbeelding van de speler. Voor spelers waarvan de tegel de hoes
  niet mag laden.

## 0.7.1 - 2026-10-15

- Reparatie: de build mislukte met „Component not found: now_playing”, omdat `plugin.yaml` nog het oude component
  noemde. Daar staat nu `scmt`, net als in het manifest en de map.

## 0.7.0 - 2026-10-15

- De id van de plugin is nu `scmt` (eerder `now_playing`), net als de map en het component. De app ziet een nieuwe
  plugin: verwijder de oude van het scherm, voeg deze toe en plaats de tegels opnieuw.

## 0.6.0 - 2026-10-15

- De plugin heet SCMT (Simple Customizable Media Tile). De id, `now_playing`, blijft, dus tegels die al op een scherm

- Nieuwe optie „Hoogte van de voortgangsbalk” (2 tot 16 pixels, standaard 4).

## 0.5.0 - 2026-10-15

- Nieuwe opties: „Spoelen door op de balk te tikken”, „Dempen”, „Volumebalk” (een tik stelt het volume in), „Albumnaam”
  (een derde regel).
- Nieuwe optie „Grote volumeweergave”: drie seconden na een wijziging ligt een half doorzichtige weergave over de hele
  tegel, met het getal in grote cijfers en een luidspreker erachter. Ook de kleine volumeweergave heeft een luidspreker.
- De tegel kan tot 4x4 cellen groot zijn (de editor biedt aan wat in het raster van het scherm past).
- Vraagt drie extra acties: `media_seek`, `volume_mute`, `volume_set`.

## 0.4.1 - 2026-10-14

- Reparatie: het manifest werd geweigerd omdat de keuzewaarde `off` als waarheidswaarde werd gelezen; elke keuzewaarde

## 0.4.0 - 2026-10-14

- Nieuw: de optie „Voortgang” kiest nu een balk, de tijd (1:36 / 7:36), beide of niets.

## 0.3.2 - 2026-10-14

- De knoppen in de tegel hebben een lichte rand.

## 0.3.1 - 2026-10-14

- De plek voor de hoes wordt alleen getoond als de speler een afbeelding heeft die het scherm mag laden; anders neemt de
  tekst de hele breedte en blijft er geen leeg grijs vierkant over.

## 0.3.0 - 2026-10-14

- Nieuw: de albumhoes naast de titel (optie „Albumhoes”), vanaf twee cellen breed, op schermen die afbeeldingen tonen.

## 0.1.1 - 2026-10-14

- Reparatie: de build mislukte omdat de kleuren als `tessera::theme::` waren geschreven; het is `theme::`.

- Eerste versie: toont titel en artiest van een mediaspeler.

readme.en:
# Status

Any Home Assistant entity as a state on a tile: a window, a door, a light, a lock, motion, a leak. The icon changes
with the state (an open or closed window, a light on or off), and so does the colour: an open window red, a closed one
green, a light that is on yellow. Use the tile as often as you like, each with its own entity, on any size from
1 x 1 to 4 x 2: square, the circle above and the words under it; wide, the circle beside them.

Everything is set on the tile itself, in the layout's inspector, without a build:

- **Entity**: a binary sensor, sensor, switch, light, input boolean, lock, cover or fan. A group works too, such as
  `binary_sensor.group_windows`, which is on while any window is open.
- **What it is**: window, door, garage door, gate, blinds, light, plug, motion, presence, lock, leak, smoke, appliance,
  alarm, switch, temperature or humidity. Its icons and words. **Auto** takes it from the entity's device class.
- **Colour when on** and **Colour when off**: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, the accent, or grey for none.
  **Auto** takes the kind's.
- **Word when on** and **Word when off**: your own, such as "All closed"; empty takes the kind's.
- **Tint the tile**: the whole tile takes the colour lightly while the entity is on.
- **Show the name**, and **Switch on a tap** for a light, a switch or a cover.

A sensor with a number shows it with its unit.

## Set up

1. In Tessera, open **Plugins**, **Add with a link**, and paste the link of this repository. Add the plugin to a
   screen and build it once.
2. In **Layout**, place a **Status** tile, choose its entity in the inspector and set what it is and its colours.
   Place as many as you like.
3. For **Switch on a tap**, the screen must be allowed to perform actions (Home Assistant, the ESPHome device's
   options).

## Good to know

- One entity per tile. For several windows at once, make a group in Home Assistant (Settings, Helpers, Group) and
  choose the group.

readme.en:
# Public transport (SE) for Tessera

![Public transport (SE) showing Swedish departures on Tessera screens](store.png)

[Svenska](README.sv.md) · [Changelog](CHANGELOG.md) · [Validation](VALIDATION.md)

Swedish public transport departures on Tessera ESP32 screens, using Trafiklab Timetables.
Install once and add multiple tiles, each with its own stop, one to eight selected lines, transport mode and optional destination.
These instructions describe plugin **0.2.2**. Swedish and English translations are included. This beta requires Tessera plugin API 0.12 (Tessera 0.4.89 / firmware 0.57.0 or later compatible versions).

## Set up

1. Register an account at https://trafiklab.se.
2. Create a key for **Trafiklab Realtime APIs** at https://developer.trafiklab.se/. A ResRobot key is a different product.
3. In Tessera, open Plugins, choose **Add with a link**, and enter https://github.com/ExhaleSthlm/tessera-plugin-sweden-public-transport.
4. Add the plugin to the intended screen, then build and install its firmware. Adding the plugin to the list alone does not install its code on the screen.
5. Enter the API key in the plugin's secret **Trafiklab API key** input. Never put it in YAML or Git.
6. Add a **Departures** tile in Layout. Open **Stop**, type at least two characters, and select a result. Its name stays visible after searching.
7. Under **Lines**, add one to eight lines from that stop. Remove a selection with ×. Select the transport mode and, optionally, an exact destination.
8. Save and send the layout. Wide tiles show a departure list, including the Guition 1×3 grid; narrow tiles emphasize the next departure.

The stop picker uses [Trafiklab Stop Lookup](https://www.trafiklab.se/api/our-apis/trafiklab-realtime-apis/stop-lookup/). It searches after a short pause while typing; Tessera caches searched choices for ten minutes. At most 48 results are offered, so use a specific name.
Line choices include each line once across both directions, using departures in the next 60 minutes; a line without departures in that window may be absent. Choices include all modes at the stop; the separate mode filter controls displayed departures. Destination text must be an exact, case-sensitive match.

At least one line is required. Removing all line selections shows **Choose lines** and stops that tile from requesting scheduled departure updates after saving the layout. Other tiles using the same stop can still keep its shared fetch active. An open editor can still request line choices. After changing stops, remove the old line selections and choose lines for the new stop; Tessera does not reset dependent selections automatically.

| Tile | Stop ID | Mode | Lines | Destination |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Blåsut metro | `740021703` | Metro | `18` | empty |
| Dalens sjukhus buses | `740065542` | Bus | `163`, `816` | empty |

The IDs above are for reference; the search picker stores them for you. Both examples show both directions. Blåsut's stop group also includes buses, so select Metro explicitly.

## Upgrading from 0.1.x or 0.2.0

Update Tessera to 0.4.89 or a later compatible version first, then update this plugin to 0.2.2 in Tessera’s Plugins view. When upgrading from 0.1.x, select the stop again in the new searchable picker. When upgrading from either 0.1.x or 0.2.0, select the lines again in the new **Lines** control; the previous two scalar line fields cannot be converted automatically by the plugin. Save/send the layout and rebuild/install the screen firmware. Existing walking time, mode, destination and delay settings keep their option IDs.

## Reading the tile

- Destination identifies the direction. The next departure counts down; larger tiles list more departures.
- `+2` means two minutes late. `TT` means timetable only, without a realtime prediction.
- Walking time hides departures you cannot reach. The countdown still shows time until departure, not time to leave home.
- Canceled departures are omitted. Empty results say “No departures”; this covers the API's next 60 minutes only.
- “Old data” means the last successful response is being shown after a fetch failure. The source credit alternates this warning and the data attribution. Both use the full footer width and are right-aligned.
- The compact source credit shows Trafiklab.se in the smallest theme text size. It sits below the departures, keeping all departure times aligned. Row spacing tightens where needed to fit three departures plus the credit on Guition 1×3. The editor's simplified preview does not reproduce every screen annotation.

## Requests and limits

Tessera fetches every 60 seconds for each distinct stop URL and shares its response between tiles of this plugin.
Two stops continuously active use an estimated 89,280 departure requests in 31 days, before editor lookups and retries. Searched stop choices are cached for ten minutes by Tessera. Line choices use the same departure URL and 60-second cache as the tile; opening them can fetch data when that cache is cold. As checked on 2026-10-18, [Realtime Bronze](https://www.trafiklab.se/api/our-apis/trafiklab-realtime-apis/#api-key-levels) allows 100,000 requests/month and 25/minute, which accommodates these two stops with some margin. More stops or other users of the same key need their own budget. This is an estimate, not an enforced account-wide cap.

The interval is currently a manifest constant. Tessera 0.4.89 has no plugin setting for runtime fetch intervals, polling schedules, or computed editor fields. See [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md) for these requested enhancements.
Each selected line filters the shared response before the results are merged, sorted and limited. The plugin sends at most the next 12 filtered departures, bounded further by Tessera's message budget; very frequent services or long walking times can exhaust this window before the next refresh.
The response must fit Tessera's 64 KiB fetch limit. Busy hubs may exceed it; filtering happens after download and cannot reduce the HTTP response size.
The two example stops returned approximately 17 KB and 9 KB during initial verification, not a guarantee for every time of day.

Trafiklab returns local timestamps without UTC offsets. They are interpreted in Europe/Stockholm. During the repeated hour when daylight saving ends, an offset-free time can be ambiguous.
Realtime availability varies by operator. Missing realtime is labeled TT, not represented as a live prediction.

## Privacy

The Tessera app in Home Assistant sends stop-name search text, selected stop IDs and the API key over HTTPS to `realtime-api.trafiklab.se`. The key is sent as a query parameter using Tessera’s secret substitution. Line, mode and destination filters are applied in Tessera after the response is downloaded.
Trafiklab sees those values and your public IP address. The key is a Tessera secret input and is never sent to the display or stored in this repository.
The plugin does not read Home Assistant entities or call Home Assistant actions.

## Data and license

Data from [Trafiklab.se](https://www.trafiklab.se/api/our-apis/trafiklab-realtime-apis/timetables/), under [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). The plugin filters and reformats the data into countdowns.
Trafiklab requires source attribution on screens and website widgets displaying this data; see the [Timetables attribution requirement](https://www.trafiklab.se/api/our-apis/trafiklab-realtime-apis/timetables/#license). This is why the tile retains a visible “Trafiklab.se” credit. The exact placement is our layout choice, not a requirement: the compact credit sits below the departure rows. Keep attribution when adapting the display. This README links the data source and license and explains the transformation above.

Plugin code is MIT licensed. The tile adapts Max Gramser's MIT-licensed `ov_departures`; its copyright and license are preserved in NOTICE.

## Development

Use Python 3.13, a C++ compiler and SDL2 (see the upstream preview setup instructions). From this plugin's repository, create fresh sibling checkouts matching CI and follow [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md):

```sh
git clone https://github.com/MaxGramser/tessera-plugins ../tessera-plugins
git -C ../tessera-plugins checkout a625674da86a6f2ba7577626407c26224ca9378c
git clone https://github.com/MaxGramser/homeassistant_espscreen ../homeassistant_espscreen
git -C ../homeassistant_espscreen checkout 9f6ab3c68d420f454fb905466696063b1d789049

export TESSERA_TREE="$(cd ../homeassistant_espscreen && pwd)"
export TESSERA_MANIFEST="$TESSERA_TREE/screen_manager/app/plugin_manifest.py"
export TESSERA_BOARDS="$TESSERA_TREE/screen_manager/app/boards.json"
python3 ../tessera-plugins/tools/preview.py --setup
export TESSERA_PYTHON="../tessera-plugins/tools/.cache/preview-venv/bin/python"
"$TESSERA_PYTHON" ../tessera-plugins/tools/check.py .
"$TESSERA_PYTHON" -m unittest discover -s tests -v
python3 ../tessera-plugins/tools/preview.py . --strict --grid 1x3
"$TESSERA_PYTHON" ../tessera-plugins/tools/store_image.py . --from .preview
```

If you already have these checkouts, use separate clean checkouts rather than replacing local work. The preview setup installs the tested ESPHome toolchain and test dependencies in its virtual environment. The core commit is the `screens-v0.4.89` release; the plugin requires API 0.12, while that core provides API 0.14.
No API key is needed for the deterministic tests and previews. Never commit credentials or raw authenticated request URLs.
Physical hardware acceptance is separate from simulator checks; see [VALIDATION.md](VALIDATION.md).

## GitHub Actions

The `Plugin CI` workflow runs on pushes, pull requests and manually from the Actions tab:

- Validates the API 0.12 manifest with Tessera 0.4.89’s API 0.14 validator and runs the deterministic mapper tests.
- Compiles the plugin C++ into the Guition host simulator and runs strict layout checks, including the 1×3 grid.
- Uploads preview images, logs and the report as the `guition-preview` artifact for seven days, including on a failed preview when files are available.

No Trafiklab API key or Home Assistant credentials are needed; tests use fixtures and make no Trafiklab calls.
The workflow has read-only repository permissions and does not publish releases or install firmware.
Tessera and its plugin tools are pinned to the commits recorded in the workflow; update them deliberately when changing the supported API.
A simulator build runs on Linux and is not an ESP32 firmware cross-build. Continue building the real Guition firmware in Tessera and testing it on the device.
Check the result for the relevant commit under [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/ExhaleSthlm/tessera-plugin-sweden-public-transport/actions); local validation is not evidence of a successful hosted run.
readme.sv:
# Public transport (SE) för Tessera

![Public transport (SE) med svenska avgångar på Tessera-skärmar](store.png)

[English](README.md) · [Ändringslogg](CHANGELOG.md) · [Testresultat](VALIDATION.md)

Avgångar från Trafiklab Timetables på din ESP32-skärm. Installera pluginen en gång och lägg till flera rutor med egna hållplatser och filter.
Anvisningarna gäller pluginversion **0.2.2**. Kräver plugin-API 0.12: Tessera 0.4.89 och skärmfirmware 0.57.0 eller senare kompatibel version.

## Installation

1. Registrera ett konto på https://trafiklab.se.
2. Skaffa en API-nyckel för **Trafiklab Realtime APIs** på https://developer.trafiklab.se/. En ResRobot-nyckel gäller en annan produkt.
3. Öppna Plugins i Tessera och lägg till länken https://github.com/ExhaleSthlm/tessera-plugin-sweden-public-transport.
4. Lägg till pluginen på skärmen, bygg och installera firmware. Att enbart lägga till pluginen i listan installerar inte dess kod på skärmen.
5. Ange API-nyckeln i pluginens hemliga inställning. Den ska inte ligga i Git eller YAML.
6. Lägg till två **Avgångar**-rutor. Öppna **Hållplats**, skriv minst två tecken och välj en träff direkt i sökningen. Namnet sparas med valet.
7. Under **Linjer**, lägg till 1–8 linjer från hållplatsen. Ta bort en vald linje med ×. Välj trafikslag enligt tabellen.
8. Spara och skicka layouten. Bredare rutor visar en lista, även Guition med 1×3-raster.

| Inställning | Blåsut tunnelbana | Dalens sjukhus buss |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Hållplats-ID | `740021703` | `740065542` |
| Trafikslag | Tunnelbana | Buss |
| Linjer | `18` | `163`, `816` |
| Destinationsfilter | Tomt | Tomt |

Hållplats-ID:n i tabellen är referenser; sökväljaren sparar dem åt dig.

Minst en linje måste väljas. Tar du bort alla visas **Välj linjer**, och rutan slutar begära schemalagda avgångsuppdateringar när layouten sparats. Andra rutor kan fortfarande hålla hämtningen för samma hållplats aktiv. En öppen editor kan fortfarande hämta linjealternativ. Linjerna delar samma avgångs-URL och 60-sekunderscache som hållplatsens övriga rutor.

Varje linje visas en gång i väljaren, oavsett riktning. Alternativen bygger på kommande 60 minuters avgångar och kan därför sakna linjer som inte går då. Alla trafikslag på hållplatsen ingår i linjevalen; trafikslagsfiltret styr avgångarna på skärmen. Vid byte av hållplats behöver du ta bort gamla linjeval och välja nya själv.

Tomt destinationsfilter visar båda riktningarna. Destinationen visas på varje rad. Blåsuts hållplatsområde innehåller även bussar, så välj Tunnelbana där.

## Uppgradering från 0.1.x eller 0.2.0

Uppdatera först Tessera till 0.4.89 eller en senare kompatibel version och uppdatera sedan denna plugin till 0.2.2 i Tesseras pluginvy. Från 0.1.x behöver du välja hållplats igen i den nya sökväljaren. Från både 0.1.x och 0.2.0 behöver du välja linjer igen under **Linjer**; pluginen kan inte automatiskt konvertera de gamla två linjefälten. Spara/skicka layouten och bygg om/installera skärmens firmware. Gångtid, trafikslag, destinationsfilter och förseningsinställning behåller sina fält-ID:n.

## På skärmen

- `+2` betyder två minuters försening.
- `TT` betyder tidtabellstid utan realtidsprognos.
- Gångtiden filtrerar bort avgångar du inte hinner till; nedräkningen visar tiden till avgång, inte tiden tills du behöver gå.
- Inställda avgångar visas inte. ”Inga avgångar” betyder att inga avgångar matchar valen och gångtiden i API:ets fönster på kommande 60 minuter.
- Källhänvisningen Trafiklab.se använder temats minsta textstorlek och ligger separat under avgångarna, så att alla tider ligger på samma lodräta linje.
- Vid hämtningsfel visas tidigare data med varningen ”Gamla tider”, växelvis med källhänvisningen Trafiklab.se. Båda texterna är högerställda och kan använda hela bredden under avgångarna.

Varje hållplats hämtas var 60:e sekund och delar svar mellan rutorna. Två hållplatser dygnet runt motsvarar cirka 89 280 avgångsanrop på 31 dagar, plus sökningar, omstarter och eventuella återförsök. Sökningen startar efter en kort skrivpaus och Tessera cachar sökträffar i tio minuter. [Realtime Brons](https://www.trafiklab.se/api/our-apis/trafiklab-realtime-apis/#api-key-levels) har enligt kontroll 2026-10-18 gränserna 100 000 anrop/månad och 25/minut; standarden ryms inom den kvoten för två hållplatser. Fler hållplatser eller andra appar med samma nyckel behöver räknas med.

Intervallet är tills vidare fast i manifestet. Inställbart intervall, dygnsschema och beräknad förbrukning i editorn kräver stöd utanför pluginens nuvarande manifest. Se [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

Pluginen är en beta. Se [engelska README](README.md#requests-and-limits) för tekniska begränsningar och [VALIDATION.md](VALIDATION.md) för genomförda tester.

## Integritet

Tessera i Home Assistant skickar sökord, hållplats-ID och API-nyckel via HTTPS till Trafiklab. Nyckeln skickas som en query-parameter med Tesseras hantering av hemliga värden. Trafiklab ser även din publika IP-adress. Nyckeln skickas inte till skärmen och sparas inte i detta repo. Linje-, trafikslags- och destinationsfilter tillämpas i Tessera efter hämtning. Pluginen läser inga Home Assistant-entiteter och anropar inga HA-tjänster.

## Varför visas Trafiklab.se?

Trafiklab kräver källhänvisning på skärmar och webbwidgets som visar deras data. Därför behåller pluginen texten **Trafiklab.se** på skärmen. Se [Trafiklabs villkor för Timetables](https://www.trafiklab.se/api/our-apis/trafiklab-realtime-apis/timetables/#license). Data omfattas av [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/); pluginen filtrerar och omformaterar uppgifterna till avgångar med nedräkning.

Kravet innebär inte att en hel rad måste reserveras för texten. Texten använder temats minsta textstorlek och ligger separat under avgångarna, så att alla tider ligger på samma lodräta linje. Behåll källhänvisningen om du anpassar layouten. Pluginens egen kod har MIT-licens; datans licens är separat.

## Automatiska kontroller med GitHub Actions

Arbetsflödet **Plugin CI** körs vid push och pull request och kan startas manuellt under **Actions**:

- Validerar pluginens API 0.12-manifest med validatorn i Tessera 0.4.89 (API 0.14) och kör testerna med exempeldata.
- Kompilerar C++-koden för Guition-simulatorn och kontrollerar layouten, inklusive rastret 1×3.
- Sparar bilder, loggar och rapport i **guition-preview**, som kan laddas ned från körningen i sju dagar.

Ingen API-nyckel behövs och inga Trafiklab-anrop görs. Arbetsflödet publicerar eller installerar ingenting. Simulatorbygget ersätter inte ett riktigt ESP32-bygge i Tessera eller test på din skärm. Kontrollera resultatet för aktuell commit under [GitHub Actions](https://github.com/ExhaleSthlm/tessera-plugin-sweden-public-transport/actions); lokala tester bekräftar inte att en GitHub-körning lyckats.

readme.en:
# Fuel prices (DE)

A tile with the prices for diesel, Super E10 and Super E5 at your petrol stations, from Home Assistant's
[Tankerkönig integration](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/tankerkoenig/). It is the idea of the Lovelace
[Tankerkönig card](https://github.com/timmaurice/lovelace-tankerkoenig-card), drawn on a Tessera screen.

The plugin asks no internet service itself: the integration already fetches the prices. One template sensor gathers
the stations you choose into lists, and the tile draws them.

**Which stations, and in which order**, you set in the template sensor: one station or up to ten.

**What the tile shows** you set per tile, in the editor's inspector:

- **Diesel**, **Super E10**, **Super E5**: each price on or off.
- **Sort by**: the order of the sensor, or the cheapest first for one fuel.
- **Only the cheapest**: just the cheapest one, two, three ... stations for that fuel.
- **Hide closed stations**, **Show the address**, **Show open or closed**, **Show price changes** (a price that went
  up turns red, one that went down green, until the next change).

On one column the tile shows the first station (the cheapest, when it sorts) with its price large. From two columns on
it is a list: a header with the fuels, and a row per station with its name, its address and a price per fuel, the tenth
of a cent small, as the price boards at the road write it.

## Set up

1. Set up the Tankerkönig integration in Home Assistant, with the stations you want, if you have not yet.
2. Copy [`home_assistant/fuel_prices_template.yaml`](home_assistant/fuel_prices_template.yaml) into your
   `configuration.yaml` (or a file it includes) and put the device ids of your stations under `stations:`. The
   file's comments say where to find them; a Tankerkönig card on a dashboard has the same ids under its `stations:`.
   Restart Home Assistant once. **Developer tools**, **States**, then shows `sensor.fuel_prices_for_screens` with the
   lists `station_names`, `station_places`, `station_open`, `diesel`, `e10` and `e5`.
3. In Tessera, open **Plugins**, **Add with a link**, and paste the link of this repository. Add the plugin to a
   screen; the screen builds.
4. In **Layout**, place the **Fuel prices** tile from the library's Plugins group, and choose the sensor in its
   inspector (only sensors with these lists are offered).
5. Choose the fuels, the sorting and the rest. The tile follows at once.

To change the stations later, edit the list in the template sensor and reload it (**Developer tools**, **YAML**,
**Template entities**): no new build of the screen.

## Station in front

**Station in front** in the inspector takes a part of a station's name or address (`JET`, `Burger`). That station
comes first: a tile of one cell shows it, a list has it on top, and the others follow sorted as set. Empty leaves the
order as it is.

## Card, one cell and top bar

- A tap on the tile opens a card with every station of the sensor: every fuel, its address, open or closed.
- A tile of one cell with two or three fuels chosen shows the station's name and a row per fuel; with one fuel, that
  price large. An arrow beside a price says how it last changed: up in red, down in green.
- The top bar item **Cheap fuel** (Top bar, Add, From plugins) says "Diesel 1,759 · JET" while the cheapest price of
  a fuel is at a limit or under. Choose the template sensor under **When building** in the plugin's details; then on
  the screen (hold the top bar, Settings, Plugins) or in the plugin's details: **Cheap fuel in the top bar** on, the
  **Fuel**, and the **Price limit** in cents (180 for 1,80 €).

## Good to know

- The tile shows a new price as soon as the integration has it (by default every 30 minutes in Home Assistant).
- A station that is closed keeps its last prices, muted. "No prices" means the station reports none right now.
- A price of 0 in the sensor means "none": the station does not sell that fuel, or has no price for it now.

## Privacy

The plugin talks to no service. Its data comes from Home Assistant, from the Tankerkönig integration you set up there.
Tankerkönig publishes the data of the German market transparency office for fuels (MTS-K) under
[CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/).

readme.en:
# Thermo dial

A tile for a climate entity with the target large, and keys to step it and change its mode. A tap on the tile opens
a card with a dial you drag, like Home Assistant's thermostat card.

## Set up

1. In Tessera, open **Plugins**, choose **Thermo dial** and tick your screens. Each screen builds once.
2. In Layout, place the **Thermo dial** tile from 1x2 up (the keys sit at the bottom).
3. Choose the `climate.*` entity in the tile's inspector.
4. Make sure the screen may perform Home Assistant actions. Tessera turns this on for a screen it added to Home Assistant;
   for a screen added by hand, tick **Allow the device to perform Home Assistant actions** in the ESPHome integration's
   options for that device.

## What it shows

- The tile: the name, the target as a number in the middle, and the keys - , mode and + below. The mode key shows only
  when the entity offers two modes or more.
- A tap on the tile, anywhere but a key, opens the card: the dial with the target large in the middle, "Now 19.8°"
  and what the thermostat is doing under it. The ring is amber while heating, blue while cooling and grey when idle or
  off.

## Good to know

- Dragging the dial changes the number only; Home Assistant gets one `climate.set_temperature` when you let go. The
  - and + keys send one after 600 ms without another tap.
- If Home Assistant does not report the new target within 5 seconds, the number goes back to the real one.
- Range and step come from the entity (`min_temp`, `max_temp`, `target_temp_step`).
- An unavailable thermostat shows a dash, and its keys and dial do nothing.

## Boards

Tried on a real screen: the Waveshare ESP32-S3-Touch-LCD-7B (7 inch, 1024x600), with a real `climate` entity: the
keys, the card and dragging its dial. Drawn by the plugin bench on the CYD, a 4-inch Guition, a 4.3-inch Waveshare and a
10-inch Guition P4, light and dark.

  key still needs two cells in width.

## 0.2.1
- Builds on Tessera 0.4.91 and later (plugin API 0.24), which took away the key and value form of `tessera::action`:
  the target and the mode go as a JSON object, the temperature as a number. The manifest names plugin API 0.12, which
  brought those fields.

  target and the temperature now, with the - and + keys and the mode key.
- The number is centred on the tile.
- The keys answer `on_tap` and `tap_point()`, so they have the screen's touch filter, not an LVGL event of their own.

- First version: a dial tile for a climate entity.

readme.en:
# Timers

A kitchen timer and a stopwatch on a Tessera screen. You set the timer with four keys that add time, **+10s**, **+1m**,
**+10m** and **+1h**, and start it: no dial to turn, no numbers to type. A ring shows how much is left, and when the time
is up its ring and time turn red and it says Done.

The timer runs on the screen itself, or as a timer helper of Home Assistant, so the same timer shows on your phone and
in your automations. The stopwatch runs on the screen and keeps the last three laps. Both keep running through a
restart of the screen.

## Set up

1. In Tessera, open Plugins and choose **Timers**, or choose **Add with a link** and paste
   `https://github.com/Heronimonimo/tessera-timers`.
2. Tick the screen in the kitchen and apply. The screen builds once.
3. In Layout, place the **Timer** or the **Stopwatch** tile from the library's Plugins group, at any size from 1x1 to
   3x3.
4. Only for a timer you want in Home Assistant too: make a timer helper first (Settings, Devices & services, Helpers,
   Create helper, Timer), then choose it as the Timer tile's entity in the inspector. Leave the entity empty for a
   timer that runs on the screen alone.

## What it shows

- **1x1**: the ring and the time. A tap opens the full-screen card with every key.
- **2x1**: the ring, the time, **+1m** and Start or Pause. A tap on the time opens the card.
- **1x2**: the ring, **+1m** and **+10m**, and the two keys that act.
- **2x2 and up, and the card**: the ring beside all four add keys, with Reset or Cancel and Start or Pause.

The timer:

- **Setting it**: tap the add keys until the time is right (2 x +1m and 3 x +10s is 2:30), then Start. Reset sets it
  back to 0:00.
- **While it runs**: the add keys add time to it; Pause and Resume, or Cancel.
- **When it is done**: its ring and time turn red and it says Done. On a screen with a speaker it rings too: three
  beeps every two seconds for a minute, or until you tap Stop. **+1m** gives it another minute, Stop ends it. A timer on the
  screen opens its card when it is done, on whatever page shows; turn that off with the setting below.

The stopwatch: Start, Pause and Resume; **Lap** while it runs, **Reset** while it is paused. The tile shows the newest
lap, the larger tiles and the card the last three.

![The plugin on the 10-inch, the 4-inch square and the CYD](store.png)

The card on the Guition 4-inch and the CYD, drawn by the real firmware on Tessera's preview bench:

![The card on the Guition 4-inch](renders/card-4inch-light.png) ![The card on the CYD](renders/card-cyd-dark.png)

Every tile at every size on the four screens of the bench: [renders/overview.png](renders/overview.png).

## In the top bar

In Layout, open a page's top bar and add **Running timer** or **Running stopwatch** from the plugins. They show only
while a timer or a stopwatch runs, in whole minutes ("6 min", "1 h 05"): the top bar looks again every five seconds,
so the tile and the card keep the seconds. A timer that is done shows a red bell and Done. With several timers the bar
shows the one that ends first, with several stopwatches the one that runs longest.

## Settings

On a screen with a speaker (from its board, such as the reTerminal D1001, or from another plugin) the plugin's details
also have the part **Ring when a timer is done**, on by default, and the setting **Timer sound**: a switch that turns
the beeps off and on again without a build, also on the screen's settings page and in Home Assistant. The beeps follow
the screen's volume.

On the screen's Plugins tab, the plugin's details, **Settings**:

- **Open the timer when it is done**: a timer on the screen opens its card when the time is up (on by default).

Home Assistant also gets a **Timer done** binary sensor of the screen: on while a timer of the screen is done. Use it
to send a notification to your phone.

## Good to know

- A timer on the screen and the stopwatch belong to their tile's place in the layout: moving a tile to another place
  starts it fresh.
- A timer helper is run by Home Assistant. Adding time to it while it runs starts it again with the new time, so its
  ring starts full again. Home Assistant's own `timer.finished` event fires as always.
- The screen counts on its own clock, which Home Assistant sets: until it is set (right after a start) a timer on the
  screen waits.
- Tried on a real screen, the M5Stack Tab5, and on the preview bench on the CYD, the Guition 4-inch, the Waveshare
  4.3-inch standing up and the Guition 10.1-inch, light and dark.

readme.en:
# Toothbrush

Your electric toothbrush live on a Tessera screen. The zones you brush show as a ring around the time: the upper jaw
on top, the lower jaw below, a zone done in green and the one you brush now in the accent. Battery, pressure and mode
sit beside it, and a tap opens the whole session over the page.

It works with the toothbrushes Home Assistant knows over Bluetooth: Oral-B (`oralb`, `oralb_live`), Philips Sonicare
(`philips_sonicare_ble`), Xiaomi (`xiaomi_ble`) and Laifen (`laifen_ble`). It is a Tessera version of
[toothbrush-card](https://github.com/mtheli/toothbrush-card) by mtheli, whose zone and session logic it follows.

## Set up

It needs a Tessera with plugin API 0.15: Tessera's dev branch until its next release.

1. In Tessera, open Plugins, choose **Add with a link** and paste this repository's link.
2. Tick the screen in the bathroom and apply. The screen builds once.
3. In Layout, place the **Toothbrush** tile from the library's Plugins group, at any size from 1x1 to 4x4.
4. In the inspector, choose the brush's entities. Only **Toothbrush** is needed; each other one adds its reading:

   | Option | Oral-B (`oralb`, `oralb_live`) | Sonicare (`philips_sonicare_ble`) | Laifen (`laifen_ble`) | Xiaomi (`xiaomi_ble`) |
   |---|---|---|---|---|
   | Toothbrush | `…_toothbrush_state` | `…_handle_state` | `…_status` | `…_toothbrush` |
   | Zone | `…_sector` | `…_sector` | leave empty | leave empty |
   | Brushing time | `…_time` | `…_brushing_time` | `…_timer` | leave empty |
   | Battery | `…_battery` | `…_battery` | `…_battery` | `…_battery` |
   | Pressure | `…_pressure` | `…_pressure_state` | `…_pressing_too_hard` | leave empty |
   | Mode | `…_mode` | `…_brushing_mode` | `…_mode` | leave empty |
   | Brush head | `…_refill_days` | brush head wear (its brush head device) | leave empty | `…_consumable` |
   | Last session | `…_last_session` | `…_last_session` | leave empty | `…_score` |

   The lists are searchable: type the brush's name. Another choice shows at once, without a build.
5. Check the other options: the number of zones (Auto, 4 or 6), the length of your routine, how long the result
   stays, and what the brush head counts (days, percent or sessions).

## What it shows

- **1x1**: the ring with the time in its middle.
- **2x1 and wider**: the ring on the left; the zone, how far you are and the chips on the right.
- **1x2 and taller**: the ring on top; the zone, how far you are and the chips under it.
- **2x2 and up**: the name, battery, pressure and mode, and a large ring.
- **A tap**: the full-screen card, with every zone named around the ring and every reading.

After a session the ring stays green for as long as you chose ("Done"), or shows how far you got ("Stopped early").

![The plugin on the 10-inch, the 4-inch square and the CYD](store.png)

The full-screen card on a 10-inch screen, in the middle of a six-zone session:

![The card on the Guition 10.1-inch, dark](renders/jc8012p4a1/card-zones-dark.png)

Every tile at every size on every screen, drawn by the real firmware on Tessera's preview bench, is in
[renders/](renders/) ([overview](renders/overview.png)): one folder per screen, light and dark, with the finest grid of
each in a folder of its own.

## Good to know

- Tessera sends the entities you choose to the screen and follows them. Nothing is needed in Home Assistant: no
  template, no helper, no integration of its own.
- Each tile has its own brush, so a screen can show several: one tile each.
- A brush without a zone sensor (Xiaomi, Laifen) gets its zones by time, evenly over the routine.
- Auto zones show 4 until the brush reports a fifth zone; choose 6 for a brush that brushes in six from the start.
- Tried on: Tessera's preview bench (the CYD, the Guition 4-inch, the Waveshare 4.3-inch standing up and the Guition
  10.1-inch), not yet on a real screen with a real brush. Please say in an issue which board and brush you used.

## Privacy

It talks to nothing outside your home: Tessera sends the screen the states of the entities you chose in the tile's
options, from your Home Assistant.

# Changelog

## 0.4.0
- The brush's entities are the tile's options now (plugin API 0.15): choose the toothbrush, and its other entities
  for the readings you want, in the tile's inspector. Tessera sends them and follows them; another choice needs no
  build and no restart.
- Each tile has its own brush, so one screen can show several.
- Needs a Tessera with plugin API 0.15 (its dev branch until the next release).
- Update: the toothbrush input and the entity settings are gone; choose the same entities in each tile's options.

## 0.3.0
- One field when you add the plugin: the toothbrush. Tessera asks for every field it shows, so the other seven are
  gone from there, and the plugin can be applied with the toothbrush alone.
- Another entity for a reading is now a setting: the plugin's details on the screen's Plugins tab, On this screen.
  Leave it empty to find it beside the toothbrush; the screen restarts once when you change one.
- Update: if you filled in the other fields before, fill the same entity ids into the settings.

## 0.2.1
- A wide tile on a small screen shows only the lines that fit: the zone first, then the name, a line of detail and the
  chips.
- A small ring shows the timer's icon where a word would not fit.
- The names around the card's ring are the side alone (Left, Front, Right), and go away where even those would crowd
  the ring.
- Tried on the preview bench: the CYD, the Guition 4-inch, the Waveshare 4.3-inch standing up and the Guition 10.1-inch,
  light and dark, on their own grids and the finest ones.

## 0.2.0
- Choose your toothbrush once: pick its main entity, and the plugin finds the brush's other entities itself (Oral-B,
  Sonicare, Laifen and Xiaomi, by their English entity names).
- The other inputs are optional now: fill one in only when your entity has another name (a Home Assistant in another
  language, a renamed entity, or a Sonicare's brush head).
- Update: open the plugin's details on the screen's Plugins tab, choose the toothbrush entity, and build once.

## 0.1.0
- First version: your electric toothbrush live on a tile, with the zones as a ring of 4 or 6 arcs, the time, battery
  and pressure, and a full-screen card with every reading.
- Reads the brush's own entities directly: choose them when you add the plugin to a screen. Nothing to set up in Home
  Assistant.

readme.en:
# Waste overview

Every kind of waste of a calendar in Home Assistant side by side on one tile: its icon in its colour, its name, and how
many days until it goes out next ("Tomorrow", "In 9 days"), the soonest first. It is the idea of the Lovelace
[trash-card](https://github.com/idaho/hassio-trash-card), drawn on a Tessera screen.

On a wide tile the kinds stand side by side, as many as fit; on a tall one they are rows, with the days at the right.

The icon and colour follow the words calendars use: paper blue, the yellow bag and packaging amber, organic waste
green, hazardous waste purple, a Christmas tree green, everything else a grey bin. German, English and Dutch words
work.

## Set up

1. Have a calendar with the collection days in Home Assistant. [Waste Collection Schedule](https://github.com/mampfes/hacs_waste_collection_schedule)
   makes one for most councils; a Local Calendar with the days typed in works too.
2. In Tessera, open **Plugins**, **Add with a link**, and paste the link of this repository. Add the plugin to a
   screen and choose the calendar under **Waste calendar**. The screen builds once.
3. In **Layout**, place the **Waste overview** tile from the library's Plugins group (4 x 1 shows four kinds side by
   side) and choose the calendar in its inspector.
4. That is all: every event name of the calendar is a kind of its own. To group or rename them, fill in the kinds
   below.

## Options

- **Days ahead**: how far ahead to look, 35 days by default. A kind collected less often than that does not show.
- **Today's collection until**: from this hour on (10 by default) a collection of today makes way for the next one of
  its kind, as the bin is out already. 24 keeps it all day.
- **Kind 1 to 5, word and name**: renames and groups kinds. Every event whose name holds the word shows under the
  name: `Rest` with the name `Restmüll` turns "Restmülltonne 2-wöchentlich" into "Restmüll", and `Gelb` with
  `Gelber Sack` puts "Gelbe Tonne" and "Gelber Sack" together. Every other event keeps its own name.

## Coming collections

A tap on the tile opens a card with the coming collections of five weeks: each with its icon, its name (renamed as on
the tile), its date and how far away.

## Good to know

- The tile asks Home Assistant for the coming events through Tessera (`calendar.get_events`): when it appears, when
  the calendar's next event changes, and every hour.
- Up to eight kinds and 24 coming collections; an answer of Home Assistant is at most about 3 KB, so a calendar with
  long descriptions may lose its last collections. Fewer **Days ahead** helps then.
- Works on every board, the CYD included.

readme.en:
# Waze travel time

Your travel time from Waze on a Tessera screen: how long the trip takes now, how far that is off your usual time, the
route Waze picks and when you arrive, with a line of how the travel time went over the last hours. A tap opens a card
with the routes Waze offers right now (up to six), fastest first.

It reads a sensor of Home Assistant's own [Waze Travel Time](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/waze_travel_time)
integration. No key, no account and no web service of its own: Home Assistant asks Waze, the plugin asks Home Assistant.

## Set up

1. In Home Assistant, add the **Waze Travel Time** integration (Settings, Devices and services, Add integration) with
   your two places, for example `zone.home` and your work address. It makes a sensor such as
   `sensor.home_to_work`. Keep the **Recorder** on for it (it is by default): the line on the tile comes from its
   history.
2. In Tessera, open **Plugins** and choose **Waze travel time**, or choose **Add with a link** and paste
   `https://github.com/Heronimonimo/tessera-waze-traveltime`. Tick your screens and choose the **Waze sensor for the
   top bar** (asked once per screen, also when you don't use the top bar); each screen builds once with the plugin.
3. Put the tile **Travel time** on a page, at any size from 1x1 to 4x4, and choose the Waze sensor in its inspector.
4. In the inspector, set:
   - **Usual travel time**: your time without traffic, in minutes. The tile then shows the delay ("+8") in green,
     amber or red, and the line gets a dashed line at that time. Leave it at 0 for no delay.
   - **Hours on the line**: how far back the line goes, 1 to 8 hours (0 for no line).
   - **Waze region**: the same region as your Waze Travel Time integration, for the routes on the card.
5. Optional: add **Travel time** to a page's top bar (Top bar, Add, From plugins). It shows the sensor you chose in
   step 2. For a coloured car, set the usual time: hold the top bar, then **Settings**, **Plugins**, **Waze travel
   time**, **Usual travel time**, or the entity **Waze usual time** of the screen in Home Assistant.

## On the screen

- **1x1**: the minutes, the delay top right, and when you arrive.
- **2x1**: the same, with the route ("via A12").
- **2 rows or more**: the line of the last hours under it, in green, amber or red by the delay now (the accent colour
  without a usual time), and the usual time dashed.
- **Tap**: the card with the routes Waze offers now, as many as fit (up to six), each with its time, a bar, its distance and how much slower it is
  than the fastest.
- **Top bar**: "23 min" beside the page's name, or "23 min +8" when it is slower than the usual time, with the car in
  green, amber or red by the delay (grey without a usual time). Hidden while the sensor has no travel time. A page can
  show its icon alone.

## Good to know

- The line comes from the sensor's history in Home Assistant (`history/history_during_period`), asked once when the
  tile is made; every new travel time after that is added on the screen. The sensor updates every 5 minutes by
  default, so the line moves in steps of about 5 minutes.
- The card asks Waze through Home Assistant's `waze_travel_time.get_travel_times` action each time it opens, with live
  traffic. It uses the sensor's own start and end, but not the sensor's other options (avoid tolls, filters). Distances
  on the card are in km.
- Waze Travel Time is an unofficial client of Waze's live map: when Waze changes something, the integration (and so
  this plugin) may stop until Home Assistant fixes it.
- Works on every board, the CYD included: it shows no pictures.
- Tried on Tessera's preview bench (the CYD, the Guition 4-inch, the Waveshare 4.3-inch standing up and the Guition
  10.1-inch, light and dark), not yet on a real screen. Found something wrong? Open an issue.

## Privacy

The plugin itself reaches nothing outside your home: the screen talks to Home Assistant only. Home Assistant's Waze
Travel Time integration asks Waze's live map for the travel time, every 5 minutes, and once more each time the card
opens. Waze then sees the two ends of your trip (often your home and your work, as coordinates) and the address of your
Home Assistant. No account, key or other personal data is sent. What Waze does with it is in
[Waze's privacy policy](https://www.waze.com/legal/privacy).

## How it works

- `tessera-plugin.yaml`: a tile of a sensor with the attributes `route`, `distance`, `origin` and `destination`, a card,
  a top bar item, the input that chooses the top bar's sensor, the setting of its usual time, and the two Home Assistant
  commands it may ask, with the history mapped to two lists of numbers.
- `plugin.yaml`: a `homeassistant` sensor that reads the chosen sensor for the top bar, and the usual time as a
  template number.
- `components/waze_traveltime/`: the tile (the line is drawn on the screen from the samples), the card, the top bar
  item, the settings row, and the plugin that hands each answer to the tile or card that asked.

readme.en:
# Weather warnings

Warnings of the DWD and NINA from Home Assistant on one tile, in the spirit of the Lovelace
[nina-dwd-card](https://github.com/timmaurice/lovelace-nina-dwd-card).

**The tile** (1 x 1 and up) shows the strongest warning in force: its icon (thunderstorm, wind, rain, snow, ice, fog,
heat ...) in a circle of its level's colour, its short name ("Sturmböen") and until when it lasts, and "+2" when there
are more. The tile itself takes the level's colour lightly: yellow for a weather warning, orange for notable weather,
red for severe weather, purple for extreme weather. NINA's severities count the same (Minor, Moderate, Severe,
Extreme). Without a warning it shows a quiet shield and "No warnings", or the DWD's advance warning, muted.

**A tap** opens a card with every warning, the strongest first and the advance warning last: a bar in its level's
colour, its icon and headline, when it is in force and where it comes from, and its text in as many lines as fit.

## Set up

1. Have the [DWD Weather Warnings](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/dwd_weather_warnings/) integration for
   your region (sensors `..._current_warning_level` and `..._advance_warning_level`) and, if you like, the
   [NINA](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/nina/) integration (binary sensors `binary_sensor.warning_<place>_1`
   and so on).
2. In Tessera, open **Plugins**, **Add with a link**, and paste the link of this repository. Add the plugin to a
   screen.
3. In the plugin's details on the screen's Plugins tab, under **When building**, choose **DWD current warning level**,
   **DWD advance warning level** and up to two **NINA warning** slots; leave out what you do not use. **Save and
   build**.
4. In **Layout**, place the **Weather warnings** tile.

## Good to know

- The screen reads the sensors and their attributes itself; a change of the chosen entities builds the screen again.
- The DWD's first three warnings, its first advance warning and two NINA slots are shown.
- Without a time the tile names the source ("DWD", "NINA"). A DWD level whose warnings have no details (yet) shows as
  "Warning level 1".

## NINA with headline and times

Newer Home Assistant versions give NINA's binary sensors only the attribute `id`; the headline, severity, text and
times come from the action `nina.get_details`. Without them the tile shows "NINA warning" in its colour. A template
binary sensor brings them back as attributes; choose it instead of the NINA sensor in the plugin's details. Put it in
`configuration.yaml` (or a file of your `template:` folder), with your sensor in place of
`binary_sensor.warning_place_1`, once per slot:

```yaml
template:
  - triggers:
      - trigger: state
        entity_id: binary_sensor.warning_place_1
      - trigger: homeassistant
        event: start
      - trigger: time_pattern
        minutes: "/10"
    actions:
      - action: nina.get_details
        target:
          entity_id: binary_sensor.warning_place_1
        response_variable: nina
        continue_on_error: true
    binary_sensor:
      - name: NINA warning details 1
        unique_id: nina_warning_details_1
        state: "{{ is_state('binary_sensor.warning_place_1', 'on') }}"
        attributes:
          headline: "{{ ((nina | default({}, true)).get('binary_sensor.warning_place_1') or {}).get('headline', '') }}"
          severity: "{{ ((nina | default({}, true)).get('binary_sensor.warning_place_1') or {}).get('severity', '') }}"
          description: "{{ ((nina | default({}, true)).get('binary_sensor.warning_place_1') or {}).get('description', '') }}"
          start: "{{ ((nina | default({}, true)).get('binary_sensor.warning_place_1') or {}).get('start', '') }}"
          expires: "{{ ((nina | default({}, true)).get('binary_sensor.warning_place_1') or {}).get('expires', '') }}"
```

readme.en:
# Wi-Fi QR

A Tessera tile that shows a scannable QR code for a Wi-Fi network. Its network name and password come from two Home
Assistant `input_text` helpers, so changing either helper updates the tile without rebuilding the screen.

## Set up

1. In Home Assistant, create two Text helpers named `WIFI_SSID` and `WIFI_PASSWORD`.
2. Put the Wi-Fi network name in `WIFI_SSID` and its password in `WIFI_PASSWORD`.
3. Add this plugin to a screen in Tessera. Choose those two helpers when Tessera asks for them, then build the screen.
4. In Layout, place the **Wi-Fi QR** tile from the Plugins group and resize it from 1 x 1 up to 3 x 3. A size of at
   least 2 x 2 is recommended for reliable scanning.

## Good to know

- The QR code uses the common `WIFI:` format with WPA security. Modern Android and iOS cameras can scan it directly.
- The password is sent to the screen through ESPHome's Home Assistant connection. It is encoded in the QR code but is
  never printed as text on the display.
- Anyone who can see the tile can join the network. Put it only on screens and pages intended for guests.
- Hidden or open networks and WEP are not supported in this first version.
